group.passage: Few objects are as ordinary as the thin plastic bag that carries groceries home. Yet this everyday item is younger than many of the people who use it, and its brief history shows how quickly a convenient invention can turn into a global headache. The material behind the bag was discovered by chance. In 1933, polyethylene was produced on an industrial scale for the first time, by accident, at a factory in the English town of Northwich, and its early wartime uses were kept secret by the British armed forces. The bag itself arrived much later. In 1965, the Swedish company Celloplast patented a one-piece shopping bag designed by its engineer Sten Gustaf Thulin. Made from a single thin sheet of plastic, it was cheap, light and surprisingly strong. Shoppers and stores quickly embraced the new bag. By 1979, four out of every five bags used in Europe were plastic. In 1982, two major American grocery chains, Safeway and Kroger, switched from paper to plastic, and other stores soon followed. Before the decade was over, paper bags had almost vanished from checkout counters around the world. Meanwhile, as the chart shows, the world's total output of plastic kept climbing. The success, however, came at a price. Discarded bags have since turned up everywhere from the deep sea to the top of Mount Everest. In 1997, a sailor and researcher discovered a vast area of floating plastic waste in the Pacific Ocean, now known as the Great Pacific Garbage Patch. In 2002, after discarded bags were blamed for choking drains during severe floods, Bangladesh became the first country to ban thin plastic bags. This turned out to be only the beginning: by July 2018, a United Nations review found that 127 of the 192 countries it examined had passed national laws on plastic bags. Today, the plastic bag is a symbol of a much larger problem. By 2019, the world was producing about 460 million tonnes of plastic a year, around 230 times the amount made in 1950. An object designed to make shopping easier now reminds us that the true cost of an invention may only become clear decades later.

translation_zh.text:
塑膠袋的誕生與代價

很少有東西像把雜貨提回家的薄塑膠袋那麼普通。然而這個日常用品比許多使用它的人還要年輕，而它短短的歷史顯示，一項方便的發明可以多快變成全球性的頭痛問題。

塑膠袋背後的材料是偶然發現的。1933 年，英格蘭諾斯威治鎮的一座工廠意外地首次以工業規模生產出聚乙烯，而它早期在戰時的用途被英國軍方列為機密。塑膠袋本身則晚了許多才出現。1965 年，瑞典公司 Celloplast 為該公司工程師斯滕‧古斯塔夫‧圖林設計的一體成形購物袋取得專利。它以單一一片薄塑膠製成，便宜、輕巧，而且出奇地堅固。

顧客和商店很快就接受了這種新袋子。到了 1979 年，歐洲使用的袋子每五個就有四個是塑膠袋。1982 年，美國兩大連鎖超市 Safeway 和 Kroger 從紙袋改用塑膠袋，其他商店也很快跟進。在那十年結束之前，紙袋幾乎從全世界的結帳櫃台消失。同時，如圖表所示，全世界塑膠的總產量持續攀升。

然而，成功是有代價的。從那之後，被丟棄的塑膠袋從深海到聖母峰頂都有人發現。1997 年，一位水手兼研究者在太平洋發現一大片漂浮的塑膠垃圾，也就是現在所稱的「太平洋垃圾帶」。2002 年，在被丟棄的塑膠袋被認為在嚴重水災期間堵塞排水溝之後，孟加拉成為全世界第一個禁止薄塑膠袋的國家。這後來證明只是個開始：到了 2018 年 7 月，聯合國的一項調查發現，在它檢視的 192 個國家中，有 127 國已通過管制塑膠袋的全國性法律。

今天，塑膠袋象徵著一個大得多的問題。到了 2019 年，全世界每年生產約 4 億 6 千萬公噸的塑膠，大約是 1950 年產量的 230 倍。一樣原本設計來讓購物更方便的東西，如今提醒我們：一項發明真正的代價，可能要到數十年後才看得清楚。

open_tasks.prompt: Some places ban thin plastic bags, while others charge shoppers for each bag. Which way do you think works better for your town? Answer in one or two English sentences and give one reason.

A ban works better for my town, because many bags still end up in our rivers, and a small charge is easy for people to ignore.
